description: Before-and-after measure of PAPER-95, Lois Cayley: 10 direct questions, 10 on a new subject after another one, 10 short follow-ups and 5 more precise ones after an admission. Written on 27 November 2026 from passages that no earlier question used, before any search or reply with them, and frozen. The earlier replies of the conversations were written by hand.

passageQuotes: Schlangenbad with the Cantankerous Old Lady

passageQuotes: give up our coupé at Malines

passageQuotes: my name's not Cyrus W. Hitchcock

passageQuotes: there were forty-eight of them

passageQuotes: Comte de Laroche-sur-Loiret

conversation.content: On the train from Ostend, at which station did the Count fear you might have to give up your compartment?
At Malines, he said.

items.input: When Harold and you compared colleges, which did you name as yours?
passageQuotes: Yours?' 'Girton

conversation.content: What was the name of the American who asked you to meet him at Fraunheim?
Cyrus W. Hitchcock, he was.

items.input: What did the German official finally say about your entering the race?
items.expectedOutput: That the woman could not compete.
passageQuotes: The woman cannot compete

conversation.content: What did you remember, from the college laboratory, that a blackish film like the one on the bangle might be?
Sulphide of silver, I remembered.

items.input: At the Austrian frontier, which book caused your trunks to be held back?
items.expectedOutput: A book of astronomy, Revolution of the Heavenly Bodies, taken for revolutionary literature.
passageQuotes: Revolution of the Heavenly Bodies

conversation.content: When you climbed up the rope to the top, how many nooses did you know there were?
Forty-eight, and I counted them.

items.input: Which newspaper offered to send you to Egypt to write articles?
passageQuotes: want on the Daily Telephone

conversation.content: In Florence, who did you recognise the urbane old gentleman to be?
Mr. Marmaduke Ashurst.

items.input: To which city did your arrangement with your newspaper proprietor take you from Suez?
passageQuotes: included a trip to Bombay

conversation.content: In the oasis, where had the veiled Englishwoman first been sold to a man?
To a man at Dongola, she told us.

items.input: Before the tiger hunt, what did you say you had never held in your life?
passageQuotes: I never held a gun in my born days before

conversation.content: Aboard ship, who said he had come to superintend the preparations for your reception?
The Maharajah of Moozuffernuggar.

items.input: In what did Lady Georgina say Mr. Ashurst had made his money?
passageQuotes: feathered his nest in soap and cocoa

conversation.content: At the trial, where did you say you had typed Mr. Ashurst's will?
In my office at Florence.

items.input: After your day in court, who came in a carriage to call on you, to your discomfort?
passageQuotes: with a pang that this was the Maharajah

conversation.content: On which make of typewriter did you say the suspect will had been written?
A Spread Eagle, like my own.

items.input: Behind which drawer of the desk was the secret hiding place of the real will?
items.expectedOutput: The central drawer on the left-hand side.
passageQuotes: the central drawer on the left-hand side

conversation.content: How did Lady Georgina try to reward you for saving her jewels?
With a cheque.

items.input: What did she do with it when you refused?
items.expectedOutput: She tore it up into very small pieces.
passageQuotes: she tore the cheque up into very small pieces

conversation.content: How did you leave Schlangenbad?
By the coach, on my own.

items.input: And how much money did you have in your pocket then?
passageQuotes: I quitted Schlangenbad with two pounds in pocket

conversation.content: What did Mr. Hitchcock offer you after the race?
To keep the Manitou bicycle.

items.input: What cut did you then propose on the orders you would bring him?
passageQuotes: ten per cent on all orders I brought you

conversation.content: Who admired your bicycle on the road and tried it?
Two Germans.

items.input: What price did you give them for it?
passageQuotes: The price of the palfrey is 400 marks

conversation.content: When you went to find Harold on the mountain, how did you track him?
By his footprints.

items.input: What was it about his boots that left marks?
items.expectedOutput: They were mountain boots with sharp-headed nails.
passageQuotes: mountain boots with sharp-headed nails

conversation.content: What did you think of the towns you passed on the Nile?
All the same: only the name differed.

items.input: What did you say it was just like?
passageQuotes: It was just like wall-paper

conversation.content: Whom had Lord Southminster taken on as his courier?
Higginson.

items.input: From whom had he enticed him away?
passageQuotes: I'll entice this chap away from Marmy

conversation.content: At the tiger hunt, what did your mahout cry out about you?
That the Mem Sahib was a great shikari.

items.input: And had you really fired?
items.expectedOutput: No: the rifle went off of itself.
passageQuotes: the rifle went off of itself without me

conversation.content: In Scotland, what did you answer when asked about your luggage?
That we had none.

items.input: At what time was the detective due in Edinburgh, so that you had to marry before?
passageQuotes: where he was due at 6.30

conversation.content: Whom did the solicitor threaten with prosecution to make him confess?
White.

items.input: Who did he say had forged the false will, and who had accepted it?
items.expectedOutput: Higginson forged it and Lord Southminster accepted it.
passageQuotes: Higginson forged, and Lord Southminster accepted

conversation.content: How did Lady Georgina behave when Harold paid you attention?
I'm afraid it has slipped my mind. Do ask me something more precise.

items.input: I mean her sharp hints at Schlangenbad: what sort of women did she go on about?
passageQuotes: about the ways of adventuresses

conversation.content: What happened when Harold came to see you at the chalet?
I'm afraid it has slipped my mind. Do ask me something more precise.

items.input: I mean when he asked to stay: who did you say ought to have been there to protect you two girls?
items.expectedOutput: Lady Georgina, as a matron of experience.
passageQuotes: Lady Georgina, as a matron of experience, ought to have protected us

conversation.content: What did Mr. Ashurst say about a young woman while you worked for him?
I'm afraid it has slipped my mind. Do ask me something more precise.

items.input: I mean the story of your coming to Germany, before he knew it was you: as what did he say his sister had taken you?
passageQuotes: took the young woman with her as her maid to Germany

conversation.content: What did Lord Southminster want from you?
I'm afraid it has slipped my mind. Do ask me something more precise.

items.input: I mean when he proposed and you refused: on whom did he say you were staking your money?
passageQuotes: staking your money on the wrong fellah

conversation.content: What did the lawyer make you admit in court?
I'm afraid it has slipped my mind. Do ask me something more precise.

items.input: I mean when you tried to explain your engagement: on what condition had you said you would marry Harold?
items.expectedOutput: Only if he was poor and without expectations.
passageQuotes: only marry him in case he was poor and without expectations
